items.headline: Tech Weekly: Anthropic's record settlement, defense firms dominate air show
items.summary: STORY: From Anthropic's class action settlement to the world AI conference in Shanghai... This is Tech Weekly.:: Tech WeeklyA federal judge has approved Anthropic's $1.5 billion class action settlement...the largest known in a U.S. copyright case.A group of writers sued Anthropic in 2024, arguing that the company used pirated versions of their books without permission to train its Claude AI model.The lawsuit is one of dozens brought by copyright owners against tech companies over the training of large language models.Tennessee state has claimed Instagram's design is to blame for a youth mental-health crisis.Meta Platforms went to court on Monday – one of several trials in the coming weeks...on allegations that the company's social media platforms were intentionally built to be addictive.The lawsuit claims Meta failed to disclose extensive internal research..showing Instagram could harm teens.A Meta spokesperson previously said in a statement that the company already has built-in controls to protect teens.Ongoing conflicts shaped discussions at the Farnborough Airshow, one of the world's largest aerospace and defense gatherings.The show brings together hundreds of companies across commercial aviation, propulsion and military technology...from unmanned fighter jets and hypersonic missiles to spy satellites and AI-enabled weapons systems.Defense companies made up half of a record 1,600 exhibitors at this year's show.Apple overtook Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company...reshuffling the top ranks of tech giants as investors reassess the outlook for AI.The shift in the pecking order illustrates how investors are looking beyond the most obvious beneficiaries of the AI boom, such as Nvidia.The 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference kicked off in Shanghai...showcasing the shifting AI landscape with Chinese open-weight AI models making rapid gains against systems from U.S. companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic.Huawei's Atlas 950 SuperPoD large-scale AI computing system made its public debut...demonstrating China's efforts to produce tech without U.S. giant Nvidia's most advanced chips. Li Tianyi was an exhibitor at the show."We work in AI applications, which are more on the software side. As far as foundation models are concerned, I think we're still slightly behind. But it's not a gap that can't be closed. At least after visiting the exhibition today, I feel confident that we can catch up with the U.S. in terms of foundation model capabilities within a relatively short period. Perhaps three to five years."An entire hall of humanoid companies also showcased robots dancing, weight lifting and looking eerily human like.

items.headline: Meta faces Tennessee trial over Instagram allegations
items.summary: STORY: Tennessee state claims Instagram's design is to blame for a youth mental-health crisis.Meta Platforms goes to court on Monday – one of several trials in the coming weeks...testing allegations that the company's social media platforms were intentionally built to be addictive.Tennessee accuses the company of violating the state's consumer protection law...by knowingly designing a product that drives teens to compulsive use...and misleading the public about its safety.The lawsuit, filed by the attorney general's office, claims Meta failed to disclose extensive internal research..showing Instagram could harm teens.And that it continued offering features it knew were dangerous without warning users.A Meta spokesperson said in a statement on Friday that the company already has built-in controls...to protect the hundreds of thousands of Tennessee teens who use social media every day.The company has argued the state's claims are based on the content posted on Instagram by its users...and that a federal law shields the company from liability for third-party content.The trial is slated to last for seven weeks.It's scheduled to overlap with at least two other trials against the company in courts in California.Meta faces thousands of lawsuits over similar claims in both state and federal court.Nearly every state in the country has filed claims against Meta over its platforms’ alleged impact on children.
